body.statement: On \(\mathcal M^{\beta}_{K,\varepsilon}(B_{\mathrm H})\) with \(\beta>(d_X+1)/2\), can the support-cleaned handle \(\mathfrak F\), using tensor-product B-splines of total dimension \(s_n\asymp n^{(d_X+1)/(2\beta+d_X+1)}\), be equipped with an explicit spline boundary or extension convention, a constrained likelihood parameterization, and a local likelihood-curvature inequality that jointly prove all of the following: the raw primitive \(L^2(P)\) rates for \((\widehat\pi,\widehat M_A,\widehat M_Z,\widehat f)\); essential-supremum rates strong enough that \(r_{A,\infty}+r_{Z,\infty}=o_P(\tau_{S,n})\) for some \(\tau_{S,n}=o(n^{-1/4})\); consistency of the empirical minimum-modal-gap permutation rule; and feasibility with probability tending to one of every cleaned-law half-margin restriction?  The support-cleaning rate-window lemma gives the admissible threshold window and the ensuing \(R_\Sigma\) and \(\Delta_n\) rates once the fitted likelihood and its cleaned plug-in coordinates satisfy that lemma's antecedents; no assertion that the listed \(L^2(P)\) coordinates alone imply \(R_\Sigma=O_P(\rho_n)\) or \(\Delta_n=O_P(\rho_n^2)\) is made.
body.justification: The revised question isolates the likelihood-curvature, spline approximation, primitive sup-norm, label-stability, and cleaned-feasibility facts needed for a genuine implementation theorem.
body.gap: No cited repeated-measurement or hidden-treatment sieve result directly establishes all of those facts for this support-cleaned projected score.
body.consumer: A positive resolution would turn the conditional inference theorem into a fully specified first-stage procedure for the augmented maternal-smoking analysis.

obligation.what_is_open: A proof that the specifically prescribed global tensor-product B-spline product-likelihood fit attains the required primitive and cleaned plug-in \(L^2(P)\) and essential-supremum rates, selects the modal labeling uniformly, and satisfies every cleaned half-margin with probability tending to one.
obligation.obstruction: The frozen H\"older assumptions do not specify a spline boundary or extension convention on the outcome support, a constrained likelihood chart, a local likelihood-curvature inequality, or a uniform empirical-process bound for the minimum-modal-gap selector. These are not consequences of the finite projector algebra or of support cleaning.
obligation.attempted: The deterministic thresholding map, exact-zero recovery, no-beta-min perturbation bound, conditional-zero cancellation, quadratic remainder, and admissible threshold window were all derived. Extending the earlier plug-in propagation argument to the named global likelihood still stops at the missing curvature, spline approximation, and uniform label-selection inputs.
obligation.partial_result: The deterministic part is closed.  Thresholding and renormalization use no true support, remove every true-zero cell with probability tending to one under \((r_{A,\infty}+r_{Z,\infty})/\tau_{S,n}=o_P(1)\), and perturb each measurement matrix by at most \(C_{\mathrm{reg}}(r_{\infty}+\tau_{S,n})\), without a beta-min condition.  Moreover, when \(\beta>(d_X+1)/2\) and a measurement sup-norm rate of order \(\rho_n\) is attained, any \(\tau_{S,n}=n^{-\gamma}\) with \(1/4<\gamma<\beta/(2\beta+d_X+1)\) lies between that rate and \(n^{-1/4}\).  Conditional on the cleaned plug-in antecedent \(R_\Sigma-r_A^{\mathrm c}-r_Z^{\mathrm c}=O_P(\rho_n+\tau_{S,n})\), the rate-window lemma gives \(R_\Sigma=O_P(\tau_{S,n})\) and \(\Delta_n=O_P(\tau_{S,n}^2)=o_P(n^{-1/2})\).  What remains open is obtaining the likelihood and plug-in antecedent rates, uniform label selection, and cleaned half-margin feasibility for the specifically named global spline product likelihood from the frozen H\"older membership assumptions alone.
